text:
Brayden Schenn spent 650 games in St. Louis, won a Cup there in 2019, and is now in his first full season as an Islander at 35. On the scoresheet it is going well: 18 points in 25 games, a 2.60 points per 60 minutes pace, and he still plays 16 and a half minutes a night with an edge (54 hits).

Underneath, it is mostly luck. The Islanders have scored 8.6 more goals than their chances deserve with Schenn on the ice, one of the biggest such gaps in the league, and his scoring rate sits above the top of our talent range. At five on five, New York has only 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, more than seven points worse than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level last season.

His own finishing is fine, six goals on 6.2 expected, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with clean exits. But one goal in his last ten games, with only 1.6 expected, suggests the shooting chances are drying up. Our talent range puts his real scoring rate closer to 2.0 per 60.
